Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — helpful session. Two quick clarifications from our side so your team can prioritize probes:

- Primary objective: replace current hyperscaler inference endpoint for customer-facing summarization flows and reduce per-token cost by >=20% while maintaining or improving hallucination rate (we measure as any fabricated factual assertions per 1k responses).

- Must-haves for POC: no PII leakage in logs, model variant must support streaming, and we need a simple canary rollback plan.

Can you send a prioritized list of probes (short sanity checks -> regression checks -> stress tests) and an initial prompt suite we can run in our sandbox? Also confirm whether you can sign a short data processing addendum for the sample prompts.

Appreciate it — Alex

Per our call, attached is a first cut: prompt-suite-v1.csv (sanity/regression/hallucination probes) and eval-matrix-v1.xlsx (priority + measurement plan). I also attached demo-logs-20260504.zip containing the short sample traces we captured from the demo environment.

High-level proposed probe prioritization (short summary):
1) Sanity suite (low effort, run now): 200 prompts across extractive QA + summarization + instruction-following to check output shape, streaming support, and basic latency.
2) Hallucination focused (medium): 1k targeted prompts, adversarial facts + domain-specific entities to measure false assertions and model tendency to fabricate.
3) Regression & consistency (medium-high): repeated prompts with minor perturbations to evaluate stability and top-k response variance.
4) Scale/stress (high): concurrent 100 req/s for 30 minutes to validate queuing/batching behavior and p95 under load.

For each probe we’ll report: median latency, p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, hallucination rate (as %), and a short example set of failure responses. We propose the initial run in your sandbox this week, then a focused hallucination sweep next week.

Next steps / asks (owned):
- BluePeak: confirm sandbox access and data processing addendum (Alex) — target: EOD Tue 2026-05-05.
- Redwood: run sanity suite and return initial report (Jonas) — target: Wed 2026-05-06.
- Redwood research: flag any prompt patterns that trigger obvious degenerative behavior and add to the adversarial list (Laura) — target: Wed 2026-05-06.

Notes on differentiators (short):
- We’ll compare both model variants and runtime configs: quantized (int8) vs fp16; batched inference with prefix caching vs unbatched baseline. Early expectation: caching gives better p95 for short conversational flows while batching improves cost for high throughput.
- We can enable canary routing so a subset of traffic uses Redwood while the rest stays on hyperscaler for live A/B.

Alex / team — quick technical addendum to Jonas’s plan so BluePeak’s engineers know what to collect. I’m copying the exact data points we need for fair comparison and the minimal instrumentation instructions.

Instrumentation / metrics to collect (per probe):
- request_id, model_variant, runtime_config (quantized|fp16|batch_size), input_tokens, output_tokens, token_cost_estimate, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, HTTP status, any error code, hallucination_flag (manual label), truncated_flag.
- For hallucination labeling: we recommend a 3-person annotation for each flagged response and majority vote to reduce noise. We’ll provide a small annotation UI if helpful.

Suggested evaluation thresholds (initial):
- Acceptable hallucination rate <= 3.0% for the 1k targeted sample.
- p95 latency for interactive flows <= 800ms.
- Cost reduction target >= 20% vs your hyperscaler baseline (we’ll compute exact cost using tokens * runtime config unit prices).

Regression checks we’ll run automatically after initial runs:
- Prompt-flip stability (50 permutations per prompt) to detect brittle generation.
- Reference-groundedness check for entity-heavy prompts (extract named entities and verify against knowledge base).
- Output length variability and abrupt truncation checks.

We’ve uploaded a working sheet with the expected CSV schema: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBluePeakPOC (see file: bp-eval-schema.csv). If BluePeak’s infra can emit logs in that schema we’ll be able to run head-to-head comparisons in our evaluation harness.

If legal needs a DPA sign-off for the sample prompts, loop in legal@bluepeak and we’ll expedite.

—Laura Bennett
